text.title: Go Error Handling Patterns (Wrap, Translate, Sentinel, Log-Once) Core Rules
text.summary: 10 testable rules every Go Error Handling Patterns (Wrap, Translate, Sentinel, Log-Once) application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Each layer wraps the error exactly once with a verb-context message: `fmt.Errorf("create user: %w", err)`.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: errorlint docs. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Repository MUST translate driver sentinels (`sql.ErrNoRows`, `redis.Nil`) into domain sentinels.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Internal reviews. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: ONE shared `apperror` package holds the canonical sentinel set (`ErrNotFound`, `ErrConflict`, `ErrUnauthorized`, `ErrValidation`, `ErrSystem`); sentinel vars per feature live in the feature package but import from apperror.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Internal reviews. Sentinels scattered across packages duplicate each other, and the edge translator needs exactly one canonical set to switch on. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Compare errors with `errors.Is` (sentinels) / `errors.As` (typed errors carrying data), never `err == ErrX` after wrapping and never a type assertion `err.(*SomeError)`.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go 1.13 release notes. `errors.Is`/`As` walk the wrap chain; equality and type assertion match only the outermost value and silently miss everything wrapped beneath it. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Log only at the outermost handler; lower layers return wrapped errors.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Internal log-volume reviews. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Returns MUST handle the error — no `_, _ = func()`; CI gate via errcheck.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: errcheck docs. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Sentinels MUST be typed (`var ErrNotFound = errors.New(...)`), never compared by `err.Error() == "..."`.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go anti-patterns. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: `panic` is reserved for unrecoverable programmer error — an invariant violation, or a must-have config missing at startup. It MUST NEVER signal a recoverable domain error (not-found, conflict, validation).
rule.rationale: Panic-as-control-flow makes the error path invisible to compiler analysis and to every reader of the function signature; it then surfaces unpredictably in production as a recovered blank 500. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Translation from domain error to HTTP status / gRPC code happens in EXACTLY ONE place — one middleware or one interceptor. Handlers return Go errors; per-handler status mapping is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Per-handler translation accumulates inconsistencies that customers see as an incoherent API (one endpoint 404, another 410 for the same condition). A single translator is auditable and changeable in one edit. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: `golangci-lint` MUST enable `errorlint` (errorf / asserts / comparison) and `wrapcheck`, alongside `errcheck`. Adapter code bridging a legacy error model goes on an explicit allowlist, never a blanket disable.
rule.rationale: These rules are only enforceable in CI — a convention document alone regresses within a sprint. `errorlint` is what catches `%v`-instead-of-`%w`, type assertions on errors, and `==` comparison of wrapped errors.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold and no duplicate exists.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.

rule.statement: Update the existing artefact in place (bump version, refresh last_reviewed).
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when a duplicate is found.
